legend.NATIVE: observed in an isolated QEMU run with the async worker

cuts.name: admission versus quiescence
evidence: NATIVE: guest ADMISSION_CLOSED precedes RESET_REQUESTED in every async run
cuts.overlap: SERIALIZED_BY_DESIGN: admission closure is the synchronisation edge, not a race

cuts.name: timeout versus completion
evidence: NATIVE: timeout observed; a simultaneous completion was not forced

cuts.name: completion versus reset
evidence: NATIVE: not forced (the fixture takes the timeout path)

cuts.name: IRQ versus reset
cuts.reason: the driver polls the used ring; no block interrupt handler exists

cuts.name: worker exit versus reset
evidence: NATIVE: ACCESS_EXITED inside the RESET_ENTERED..RESET_ACKNOWLEDGED interval
NATIVE: WORKER_JOINED before MAPPING_RELEASED and before acknowledgment
cuts.overlap: TRUE_OVERLAP: worker read iterations advanced during the reset critical interval

cuts.name: callback cancellation versus completion
evidence: NATIVE: async-negative shows cancellation losing to an acknowledged reset

cuts.name: mapping release versus reset acknowledgment
evidence: NATIVE: MAPPING_RELEASED seq < RESET_ACKNOWLEDGED seq in all 12 positive runs
cuts.overlap: ordered by join; the mapping is released before the acknowledgment boundary

cuts.name: reset owner versus competing reset owner
evidence: NATIVE: RESET_OWNER_CONTESTED on a distinct CPU in 2-CPU and 4-CPU runs
cuts.overlap: real SMP contention; loser is refused, winner is unique

cuts.name: late callback versus new epoch
evidence: NATIVE: no new epoch is authorised (queue-epoch remains 1)
cuts.overlap: host interleaving only; native new epoch intentionally NOT_RUN

cuts.name: device removal versus outstanding mapping
evidence: NATIVE: no device removal is exercised

cuts.name: terminal failure versus queued new I/O
cuts.overlap: closed admission refuses new I/O after a terminal outcome

cuts.name: repeated reset under resource pressure
evidence: NATIVE: PMM free-before == free-after, but no pressure is applied

not_run_reason: R4/R5 require an interrupt-driven completion path that the current driver does not have; forcing one would be a driver redesign outside this milestone.
